findings.current: The powerful defensive Magic layered throughout the area collapsed beneath the ultra-high temperature. Even the ceiling, made from exceptionally durable magical materials, melted away.
findings.defect: The source says both the layered defensive Magic and the ceiling collapsed and melted; the draft assigns only one destructive effect to each.
findings.rationale: The shared predicates 무너지고 녹아내렸다 apply to both subjects.
findings.replacement: Layer after layer of powerful defensive Magic—and even the ceiling, made from exceptionally durable magical materials—collapsed and melted beneath the extreme heat.
findings.source: 겹겹이 설치된 강력한 방어 마법도, 단단하기 그지없는 마법 재료로 만들어진 천장도 초고온의 열기에 무너지고 녹아내렸다.

findings.current: At the end of the corridor, more than a dozen healers stood with their mouths hanging open, staring at the scene before them.
findings.defect: 십여 명 means roughly ten or a dozen, not more than twelve; the draft increases the stated number.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the source's approximate quantity without imposing a minimum of thirteen.
findings.replacement: At the end of the corridor, a dozen or so healers stood with their mouths hanging open, staring at the scene before them.
findings.source: 복도의 끝에서 십여 명의 힐러가 입을 딱 벌린 채 자신들의 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경을 바라보고 있었다.

findings.current: That was why I had stopped the feet that had been about to leave.
findings.defect: The literal rendering is unnatural and obscures that Taekyung deliberately stopped instead of walking away.
findings.rationale: 굳이 emphasizes his deliberate choice to remain when he otherwise intended to leave.
findings.replacement: That was precisely why I stopped instead of simply walking away.
findings.source: 굳이 떠나려던 발걸음을 멈춘 이유는 바로 그 때문이었다.

findings.current: “I don’t think people who came swarming over to kill me because of those four letters—Code Red—have the right to say that.”
findings.defect: Code Red does not consist of four English letters; mechanically retaining the Korean character count produces a false and distracting statement.
findings.rationale: 그 네 글자 refers to the four Korean written syllable blocks in 코드 레드; “those words” preserves the rhetorical reference naturally in English.
findings.replacement: “I don’t think people who came swarming over to kill me over those words—Code Red—have any right to say that.”
findings.source: 코드 레드. 그 네 글자에 나 죽이겠다고 우르르 몰려온 인간들이 할 소린 아닌 것 같은데.

findings.current: I had always doubted what kind of person I was. I had always questioned whether my choices were right.
findings.defect: The draft changes the specific present choice into Taekyung's choices in general and loses the source's emphatic repetition of doubt.
findings.rationale: 이 선택 is singular and immediate, while 의심하고 또 의심했다 explicitly repeats the act of questioning.
findings.replacement: What kind of person was I? Was this choice right? I questioned myself again and again.
findings.source: 스스로가 어떤 사람인지. 이 선택이 맞는지 늘 의심하고 또 의심했다.

findings.current: “Please, don’t give me bullshit about not having enough money to raise your kids or living with your widowed mother. You’re not starving right now.”
findings.defect: 모시고 살다 means supporting and caring for one's widowed mother, not merely living with her; the draft weakens the hardship being invoked as an excuse.
findings.rationale: The honorific construction 모시고 살아서 presents the mother as a dependent whom the speaker must care for.
findings.replacement: “Please, don’t give me bullshit about not having enough money to raise your kids or needing to support your widowed mother. You’re not starving right now.”
findings.source: 부탁인데 애들 키울 양육비가 부족해서, 홀어머니를 모시고 살아서, 뭐 그런 개 같은 소리는 하지 마. 당신들은 지금도 그렇게 배고픈 처지가 아니잖아.

findings.current: I had once dreamed of becoming just like them.
findings.defect: The source says Taekyung once dreamed of their successful life of wealth and honor, not of becoming like these people in character.
findings.rationale: 모습 points back to the successful condition just described; “becoming just like them” implies identification with the people themselves.
findings.replacement: I had once dreamed of that kind of life myself.

findings.current: The middle-aged man had crossed the distance with lightning speed and slapped the archer on the cheek. Then he looked back at me.
findings.defect: The draft invents the man crossing a distance and omits that the archer was standing to his right.
findings.rationale: The source describes only the rapid slap and explicitly locates the archer on the man's right.
findings.replacement: The middle-aged man slapped the archer on his right across the face with lightning speed, then looked at me.
findings.source: 번개 같은 속도로 오른쪽에 있던 궁수의 뺨을 후려갈긴 중년인이 나를 바라보았다.

findings.defect: “Idiots” sanitizes the force of the deliberately harsh insult 병신들.
findings.rationale: 병신들 is a strongly offensive insult, and the surrounding narration establishes Taekyung's openly profane register.

findings.current: The statue’s face was so lifelike that I had no trouble recognizing it, despite there being no way to call it an ordinary statue.
findings.defect: The added “despite” creates a nonsensical opposition between the statue's exceptional realism and Taekyung's ability to recognize the face.
findings.rationale: The source gives two compatible facts: the statue is exceptionally lifelike, and its face is easy for Taekyung to recognize.
findings.replacement: The statue was too lifelike to be called a mere stone figure, and I recognized the face without difficulty.
findings.source: 나는 단순한 석상이라고 부를 수 없을 만큼 생동적인 석상의 얼굴을, 어렵지 않게 알아볼 수 있었다.

findings.current: “There are two choices. Put down your weapons and clear a path, or protect my back.”
findings.defect: “Protect my back” is an unnatural literal rendering of 내 뒤를 지키다 in this combat context.
findings.rationale: “Watch my back” naturally conveys the command to guard him from behind and join his side.
findings.replacement: “There are two choices. Put down your weapons and clear a path, or watch my back.”
findings.source: “둘 중 하나다. 무기를 내려놓고 길을 트던가, 그것도 아니라면 내 뒤를 지키든가.”

summary: Several localized fidelity and register issues, including one altered quantity, an invented movement, softened profanity, and a garbled description of the statue.
